taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes competing generic arrangements for American ranids (Lithobates used here).
fieldMarks: Tan back with two parallel rows of roughly rectangular dark spots (about seven pairs) plus a snout spot.
Groin and base of hind legs yellow or orange (faint or absent in juveniles).
Light stripe along upper jaw; glandular ridge down each side; hind toes extensively webbed.
Maximum about 8.7 cm snout-vent; call a low snore lasting 1-2 seconds.
behavior: Gathers at water after hibernation; in summer commonly ranges into fields and woods away from water.
Most active at night in the breeding season; hibernates in pond bottoms, caves or mines, later than the northern leopard frog.
Skin secretions are distasteful; some predators reject it.
habitat: Freshwater and wetland habitats in wooded regions, from cool clear streams and ponds in the north to warm, turbid swamps in the south; in the south and midwest often tied to limestone caves for overwintering.
range: Gaspe Peninsula of Quebec and New Brunswick/Nova Scotia west to Wisconsin and Missouri, south to South Carolina, northern Georgia, southern Mississippi and southeastern Texas; largely absent from Florida and southern Georgia.

lookalikes.name: Northern leopard frog
lookalikes.howToTell: Pickerel frog has squarish, parallel dorsal spots and a yellow-orange groin; Animal Diversity Web calls the two visually similar.
